title: Business-date operations preserve calendar, interval and adjustment context
question: Compare endpoint inclusion, signed reversal, zero offsets, vector admission, finite calendar coverage, registry state and serialization without assuming one market calendar.

evidence.title: Business-day counting and offsets express different endpoint policies
explanation: bizdays counting uses signed dual-index differences, adjustments and financial/nonfinancial endpoint corrections; offset zero explicitly restores the original input date.
The count and offset bodies have different normalization and vector-recycling contracts, so they cannot be treated as unrestricted inverses.

Selected financial flag and adjustment functions, valid calendar coverage and intended R vector shapes; offset uses rep_len while count checks divisibility. Offset zero can retain a holiday, while count adjusts endpoints; exchanging these policies with BusinessDays changes observable results. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Any-in-range guards and edge search can outlive calendar knowledge
explanation: Several public date wrappers admit a vector when any date is in range, while adjustment treats an unknown index as a terminal true result.
The any-range checks and NA-to-TRUE branch can admit partially uncovered inputs or stop a following search outside coverage. Period sums also do not verify complete month/year coverage.

explanation: The calendar save projection omits start/end coverage; loading consults those members and defaults missing financial to false, whereas create defaults financial to true.
The serializer/loader projections do not promise complete context preservation. Exact restored bounds depend on the receiving constructor and JSON representation.

evidence.title: Calendar registry exposes mutable implicit context and partial reloads
explanation: Calendar creation overwrites a named live registry entry, and QuantLib loading catches individual failures and continues without deleting an existing entry.
The exposed registry and closure-backed defaults are mutable local policy; loading is not an atomic snapshot replacement.
